column1: # The OpenID Foundation conformance suite lane's pass list (#621,
# scripts/oidf/lane.sh): every module of the four OpenID Connect plans and
# of the OpenID4VP verifier plan (#817), the PID as an SD-JWT VC and, under
# the plan name with `.iso_mdl`, as an mdoc (#793), in the order the
# suite runs them, with the result the suite gives it and, for a relying
# party module, what FerroSMART made of the provider's answer (accepted,
# refused, no-start, started; none when the module did not run), and for a
# verifier module, of the wallet's presentation (accepted, refused). A failure,
# and a login the module does not ask for, names its issue. Columns, tab
# separated: plan, module, result, login, issue (- for none), reason. A
# module whose outcome races the suite lists each outcome it can end in,
# `|` between the results and between the logins, paired by position; it
# names its issue and the race, and the badges count its first outcome.

column6: the suite skips an unsigned ID Token in the code flow; FerroSMART refused it

the module takes the access token only from the form body (RFC 6750 §2.2, a MAY) and answers 400 to the Authorization header FerroSMART sends, which RFC 6750 §2.1 has every resource server support and OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.3.1 recommends; FerroSMART refuses a login whose UserInfo request fails (§5.3.3)

the module waits for the relying party to fetch the distributed claims' source (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.6.2), which FerroSMART does not, as no claim it uses comes from one, so the driver stops the module once the login is accepted

the module finishes once the key set is read and races FerroSMART's UserInfo request (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.3): when the module has finished first it answers 400 (Illegal test state change: FINISHED -> RUNNING) and FerroSMART refuses a login whose UserInfo request fails, otherwise the login is accepted and the module passes
